title: Subscription
description: A Business-defined grouping of recurring line items that the Business places recurring orders for on the buyer's behalf, as it stands now.

id.description: Opaque, stable identifier of the subscription. Never reused for another subscription.

label.description: Human-readable label for identifying the subscription (e.g. 'Coffee, every month'). MUST only be provided by the business.

status.description: Lifecycle state of the subscription. Well-known values: `active` (recurring orders are being placed), `paused` (no recurring orders are placed until the subscription is resumed), `canceled` (the buyer or the Business ended it), `ended` (it reached the end of its last schedule). Platforms MUST tolerate unknown values and rely on `operations` for what can be done.

revision.description: Opaque token that changes whenever the subscription, or a policy or message that targets it, changes. Sent back on every operation that changes the subscription, so the operation applies only to the state the buyer saw.

permalink_url.description: Page on the Business's site where the buyer manages the subscription. The authoritative management experience, including every change this capability does not expose.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code of every amount on the subscription.

order_id.description: ID of the Order whose checkout started the subscription.

line_item_ids.description: IDs of the lines on that Order that became this subscription.

origin.description: The Order whose checkout started the subscription, and which of its lines. Present when the Business can identify it.

line_items.description: What each recurring order contains, on the terms currently in effect.

upcoming_orders.description: Recurring orders the Business plans to place, in the order it plans to place them. Empty when it plans none, as while the subscription is paused.

operations.description: Operations on the whole subscription, keyed by operation name: `pause_subscription`, `resume_subscription`, and `cancel_subscription`, plus the handoff-only `update_payment`. A key that is absent means the operation does not apply to the subscription in its current state.
